On our 3-model × 3-strategy benchmark, Random Forest classifiers on 19 statistical features achieve 70–85% four-class accuracy (chance=25%), with the best configuration (GPT-2 XL, temp τ=0.9) reaching 85.4%. Feature-based methods (RF, CORAL, DivEye) consistently outperform single-feature baselines across all 9 settings.\\n\\n2. **Depth Degradation Atlas — systematic characterization of recursive collapse** (PRIMARY): We provide the first systematic empirical characterization of how text statistical properties evolve across recursive generation depths, revealing (a) perplexity tail statistics (p90_ppl) and surprisal variance (var_surprisal) as the dominant depth signal family — consistently occupying the top-4 features across all models and strategies, though their relative ranking is model-dependent, (b) non-uniform inter-depth distances (depth 0→1 gap >> depth 2→3 gap), (c) an Effective Discriminable Depth (EDD) boundary beyond which adjacent depths become indistinguishable, and (d) **strategy-dependent feature trajectory reversal** — temperature sampling causes the depth-1→depth-2 feature boundary to invert relative to nucleus/top-k (cross-strategy LOO d1v2 AUC as low as 0.13), demonstrating that decoding strategy fundamentally shapes the degradation trajectory rather than merely attenuating it, and (e) **accelerated convergence mechanism** — root cause analysis confirms covariate shift: temperature's uniform logit scaling (vs nucleus/top-k truncation) accelerates convergence to the attractor distribution, so temp09 depth N features ≈ nucleus/topk50 depth N+1 (GPT-2 XL temp09 d1 p90_ppl median=92.2, falls into nucleus/topk50 d2 range 65–92). Z-score normalization recovers cross-strategy d1v2 AUC on feature-level / linear models (0.13→0.68 GPT-2 XL, 0.25→0.83 OLMo), but does **not** improve tree-based classifiers (RF Δ<0.02pp) — tree splits depend on rank order, not absolute values. This two-layer structure (scale shift correctable for linear methods + feature-space geometry shift uncorrectable for trees) deepens the characterization beyond simple covariate shift. This atlas spans 3 model families × 3 decoding strategies.\\n\\n3. **[Discussion — Practical Implication]** Depth-graduated curation as alternative to binary filtering: predicted depth provides a finer-grained quality proxy than binary real/synthetic labels, enabling graduated weighting strategies. Conceptual argument supported by depth-accuracy correlation in 3×3 matrix data; full experimental validation deferred to future work (D012).\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n- **Problem**: Web-scraped training corpora increasingly contain multi-generational synthetic content from uncontrolled model→data→model feedback loops. Existing detectors answer \\\"is this synthetic?\\\" but not \\\"how many recursive cycles has this undergone?\\\" — a critical distinction since 1st-gen synthetic data can improve training while deeply recursive text drives distribution collapse.\\n\\n- **Existing approaches & gaps**: Binary detectors (LOKI, DivEye, Binoculars) classify real vs. synthetic but discard ordinal depth information. EditLens estimates single-pass AI editing extent but not recursive depth. Model collapse studies (Drayson et al. EMNLP 2025; Shumailov et al. Nature 2024) characterize degradation patterns but assume depth is known a priori — no method estimates depth from text alone.\\n\\n- **Our framing**: We formalize ordinal generation depth estimation as a new task, construct a multi-generational benchmark (3 models × 3 strategies × 4 depths), and provide the first **Depth Degradation Atlas** — a systematic empirical map of how text statistical properties evolve across recursive depths, models, and strategies. The Atlas reveals (a) perplexity tail statistics as universal depth markers across all 9 settings, (b) model-dependent strategy interaction effects (temperature enhances signal for some models, attenuates for others), and (c) the Effective Discriminable Depth (EDD) boundary beyond which adjacent depths become indistinguishable. We show that feature-based classifiers achieve 70–85% four-class accuracy, demonstrating the task is non-trivial but solvable with the right feature family.\\n\\n- **Headline result template**: \\\"On our multi-generational benchmark spanning 3 model families and 3 decoding strategies, feature-based ordinal depth estimation achieves 70–85% accuracy (chance=25%), with perplexity tail statistics (p90_ppl, var_surprisal) consistently among the top-4 features across all 9 settings. The Depth Degradation Atlas reveals that effective discriminable depth extends to depth 3 in 7/9 settings (T=0.75), with model-strategy interaction effects: temperature sampling enhances signal for GPT-2 XL (+2.1pp) but attenuates it for Pythia (−1.9pp).\\\"\\n- **Note**: 4-class (depth 0-3) is the confirmed setting. 6-class (depth 0-5) pending plan_011 results.\\n\\n## DCOL Status — Contingency Activated (D010/D011, 2026-05-15)\\n\\nDCOL v1–v5 全部失败（embedding collapse / OOM / catastrophic forgetting / 超参违规 / NaN 梯度爆炸）。\\n\\n- **Claim 2 (Atlas/EDD) 升为 PRIMARY contribution**\\n- **Claim 1**: Feature-based methods (RF/CORAL/DivEye) 作为 depth estimation 方法，不依赖 DCOL\\n- **DCOL v6 (RoBERTa-large)**: 非阻塞尝试。成功 → Section 5 bonus；失败 → negative analysis section（\\\"contrastive ordinal learning 在文本深度估计的固有局限\\\"）\\n- **Paper type**: Task formalization + systematic empirical study + practical framework（非 method paper）\\n- Atlas + EDD + feature universality + model-strategy interaction = 充分支撑 EMNLP \\\"New Missions\\\" track\\n\\n## Venue Fit Risks\\n\\n- **\\\"Just an empirical study\\\" risk**: Primary risk now that DCOL is demoted. {"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# OLMo-1B depth extension: d3 → d4 → d5
# Continues from cross_model_olmo_001 checkpoints (lora_depth_0/1/2)
# Input: data/olmo/depth_3.jsonl (5000 samples from parent experiment)
# Output: data/olmo/depth_4.jsonl, depth_5.jsonl, checkpoints/olmo/lora_depth_3/4,
#         results/olmo_depth_extension/ (6-class RF/LR + binary pairwise)
# GPU: cuda:1

set -e

if [ -n "${AML_EXP_ID:-}" ]; then
    _aml_exit_handler() { local ec=$?; mkdir -p /tmp/agent-ml-exit; printf "%s|%s\n" "$ec" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" > "/tmp/agent-ml-exit/${AML_EXP_ID}.exit"; }
    trap _aml_exit_handler EXIT
fi

PROJECT_DIR="/root/autodl-tmp/recursive_gen_depth_est"
cd $PROJECT_DIR

source /etc/network_turbo 2>/dev/null || true
export HF_HOME=/root/autodl-tmp/.hf_cache
export HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1
export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt

if [ -f /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh ]; then
    source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
    conda activate base
fi

export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1

MODEL_PATH="/root/autodl-tmp/models/olmo-1b-hf"
TARGET_MODULES="q_proj,k_proj,v_proj"
DATA_DIR="data/olmo"
CKPT_DIR="checkpoints/olmo"
RESULTS_DIR="results/olmo_depth_extension"

mkdir -p "$CKPT_DIR" "$RESULTS_DIR" logs

echo "[$(date)] === Step 1: LoRA finetune on depth_3 (OLMo-1B) ==="
if [ -d "$CKPT_DIR/lora_depth_3" ] && [ -f "$CKPT_DIR/lora_depth_3/adapter_model.safetensors" ]; then
    echo "  Skipping: $CKPT_DIR/lora_depth_3 already exists"
else
    python scripts/lora_finetune.py \
        --input_data "$DATA_DIR/depth_3.jsonl" \
        --output_dir "$CKPT_DIR/lora_depth_3" \
        --model_name "$MODEL_PATH" \
        --target_modules "$TARGET_MODULES" \
        --gpu 1
fi

echo "[$(date)] === Step 2: Generate depth_4 (5000 samples) ==="
if [ -f "$DATA_DIR/depth_4.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "  Skipping: $DATA_DIR/depth_4.jsonl already exists ($(wc -l < "$DATA_DIR/depth_4.jsonl") lines)"
else
    python scripts/generate_next_depth.py \
        --adapter_dir "$CKPT_DIR/lora_depth_3" \
        --output_path "$DATA_DIR/depth_4.jsonl" \
        --target_depth 4 \
        --model_name "$MODEL_PATH" \
        --num_samples 5000 \
        --decoding_strategy nucleus \
        --top_p 0.95 \
        --max_new_tokens 512 \
        --seed 42 \
        --gpu 1
fi

echo "[$(date)] === Step 3: LoRA finetune on depth_4 ==="
if [ -d "$CKPT_DIR/lora_depth_4" ] && [ -f "$CKPT_DIR/lora_depth_4/adapter_model.safetensors" ]; then
    echo "  Skipping: $CKPT_DIR/lora_depth_4 already exists"
else
    python scripts/lora_finetune.py \
        --input_data "$DATA_DIR/depth_4.jsonl" \
        --output_dir "$CKPT_DIR/lora_depth_4" \
        --model_name "$MODEL_PATH" \
        --target_modules "$TARGET_MODULES" \
        --gpu 1
fi

echo "[$(date)] === Step 4: Generate depth_5 (5000 samples) ==="
if [ -f "$DATA_DIR/depth_5.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "  Skipping: $DATA_DIR/depth_5.jsonl already exists ($(wc -l < "$DATA_DIR/depth_5.jsonl") lines)"
else
    python scripts/generate_next_depth.py \
        --adapter_dir "$CKPT_DIR/lora_depth_4" \
        --output_path "$DATA_DIR/depth_5.jsonl" \
        --target_depth 5 \
        --model_name "$MODEL_PATH" \
        --num_samples 5000 \
        --decoding_strategy nucleus \
        --top_p 0.95 \
        --max_new_tokens 512 \
        --seed 42 \
        --gpu 1
fi

echo "[$(date)] === Step 5: Feature extraction (depth 0-5, 6-class) ==="
python scripts/extract_features.py \
    --data_dir "$DATA_DIR" \
    --model_path "$MODEL_PATH" \
    --output_path "$RESULTS_DIR/features_6class.jsonl" \
    --gpu 1 \
    --max_depth 5

echo "[$(date)] === Step 6: Train 6-class classifier ==="
python scripts/train_classifier.py \
    --features_path "$RESULTS_DIR/features_6class.jsonl" \
    --output_dir "$RESULTS_DIR/"

echo "[$(date)] === Step 7: Binary pairwise RF evaluation ==="
python src/binary_pairwise_eval.py \
    --features_path "$RESULTS_DIR/features_6class.jsonl" \
    --output_dir "$RESULTS_DIR/binary_pairwise/"

echo "[$(date)] === Step 8: Data summary ==="
wc -l "$DATA_DIR"/depth_*.jsonl
echo ""
echo "Results:"
ls -la "$RESULTS_DIR/"
ls -la "$RESULTS_DIR/binary_pairwise/" 2>/dev/null || true

echo "[$(date)] === OLMo-1B depth extension pipeline complete ==="

    if args.dry_run:
        cells_to_run = ["pythia_nucleus095"]
    elif args.cells:
        cells_to_run = args.cells
    else:
        cells_to_run = list(CELL_PATHS.keys())

    # Load 6-class data once if needed
    X_6class, y_6class = None, None
    if "pythia_nucleus095" in cells_to_run and SIXCLASS_PATH.exists():

    all_results = []
    t0 = time.time()

    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
